chunks: ʿAlī, from his father, from Ibn Maḥbūb, from Isḥāq ibn ʿAmmār, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام ruled regarding wounds in the fingers: when the bone becomes exposed, it is one-half of one-tenth of the blood-money of the finger, if the injured person does not wish to retaliate in equal measure.
ai.seo_question: What is the diyah for a finger wound that exposes the bone if the injured person does not seek qiṣāṣ?
ai.summary: This hadith records a legal ruling from Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام concerning compensation for a wound to a finger that exposes the bone. It specifies the amount of diyah due when the injured party does not choose qiṣāṣ, showing the precise treatment of bodily injury in Islamic jurisprudence.
